Sharding Walkthrough: Social Platform

Requirements to key, components, schema, routing, read/write/global flows, and an online split - end to end.

Requirements → keyComponentsSchemaFlowsSplit S3

Quick Revision

  • User-scoped reads/writes + user-owned transactions → hash(user_id) into 4096 buckets.
  • Search, trending, analytics are derived from CDC - no live fan-out.
  • Every shard group: primary + 2 replicas; epoch-versioned map.
  • Celebrities: cache/replicate, pull-based feeds, dedicated placement.
  • Split online with snapshot + CDC + epoch 44.

Flows

  • Read - user_id=8472 → bucket 392 → S3 @43 → primary (own post) or replica → indexed range query → posts + cursor.
  • Write - route to S3 primary → local transaction: post + outbox → commit → POST_CREATED → cache, search, trending, analytics update.
  • Global - CDC → aggregator/search → API. Rare fallback: bounded local top-K + merge, with complete and missingShards in the response.
  • Split S3 (384-511 → S3A 384-447, S3B 448-511) - provision → snapshot/copy → replay CDC → shadow-read → publish epoch 44 → old S3 returns MOVED → canary → S3 read-only for rollback → delete after safety window.
  • Why - user-local operations; hashing spreads ordinary users; buckets allow controlled moves; derived globals avoid fan-out; replicas give availability; outbox makes propagation reliable; epochs make stale clients visible.

Interview practice

Answer aloud, then reveal.

Why user_id and not post_id?

Dominant operations and transactions are user-scoped; post_id would scatter one user's timeline across shards.

How do trending and search work without fan-out?

Each shard's outbox/CDC feeds a streaming aggregator and a search index; global APIs read those.

How does a user see their own new post immediately?

Read from the primary or pass a minimum-version token so lagging replicas are skipped.

Why 4096 buckets for 48 shards?

~85 buckets per shard lets you move small units when adding capacity without changing the hash function.
